theme: Request body stream: ReadAsync returns 0 at end
text: For ASP.NET Core request.Body stream, ReadAsync returns 0 when there are no more bytes and the request body has ended. It does not mean 'no bytes right now' in the same way as some network polling APIs; it means end-of-stream for the request body.
code:
int read = await Request.Body.ReadAsync(buffer);
if (read == 0) { /* end */ }

text: The example shows reading request.Body in a loop into a byte buffer. Each iteration processes only buffer[..bytesRead]. When bytesRead becomes 0, the loop ends and body processing completes.

For HttpContext.Request.Body, network disconnects and client aborts can surface as exceptions such as IOException or OperationCanceledException. RequestAborted can be used as the cancellation token. If a streaming endpoint reads the body, you should handle cancellation and IO errors explicitly.

The source suggests catching request-body exceptions around streaming acquisition/iteration. Client disconnects, cancelled requests and network errors are expected runtime cases and should not be treated like normal parsing completion.

theme: Which exceptions to catch for different APIs
text: The source lists examples: HttpClient request/response phases may throw HttpRequestException; request body stream can throw IOException; ASP.NET Core request stream can throw IOException directly; WebSocket receive can throw WebSocketException rather than HttpRequestException.

HttpClient can be used in streaming mode with HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead. That avoids buffering the whole response before returning. The code gets the response stream and reads chunks in a loop into a buffer, processing each chunk as it arrives.

theme: ResponseHeadersRead means headers first, body streamed later
text: With the default completion option, HttpClient may buffer more of the response before handing control back. With ResponseHeadersRead, the operation returns after response headers and allows the body to be streamed/processed chunk by chunk.

The code shows a canonical loop: call GetAsync with ResponseHeadersRead, ensure success, read response.Content.ReadAsStreamAsync, then repeatedly ReadAsync from source stream and WriteAsync to destination stream.

ReadAsync may return any positive number of bytes up to the buffer length. You must process exactly the bytes returned. A return value of 0 means stream end. If you need exactly N bytes, use ReadExactly or accumulate until enough data exists.

theme: Practical mental model: layers and message boundaries
text: The mental model separates TCP byte stream, browser/app buffers, WebSocket message layer and app protocol. Streams deliver chunks; message boundaries may not align with read chunks. Protocol parsing must account for partial and combined messages.
code: TCP bytes -> buffers -> protocol/message layer -> app parsing
